decisions.summary: A frame(title, here, open_keys, *, lazy_glossary) function returns the text before <main>\n and from \n</main> on; shell with a string body is head + linkify(body) + tail.
decisions.why: The mechanism FR-001 needs (the page's frame without a rendered body), held to FR-002's byte identity for every shell caller; replaces the prototype's NUL split. Adds no behavior and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: shell given a list linkifies each piece in place and returns one join of head, the pieces and tail; _single passes its out list with heading and table of contents at the front; the list is consumed.
decisions.why: This is FR-001 as written: only the pieces and the finished page are held, with no joined body, linkified copy or f-string copy. Consuming the caller's list touches only _single's local list, so FR-003 holds.

decisions.summary: Linkifying per piece equals linkifying the whole because each _single piece is a whole fragment, so no link, comment, script or style spans two pieces; proven by the real-record file comparison and a unit test.
decisions.why: Restates the spec's own Assumption, measured on the prototype (R2: 2,698 files byte-identical) and held by SC-002. It does not narrow the edge case that every URL on every page is linked, because byte identity with main is the acceptance test.

decisions.summary: build still returns the path-to-text dictionary; the other shell callers pass a string.
decisions.why: This is FR-003 and the spec's edge case that the other pages are built as before.

decisions.summary: frame carries a Research NONE (process plumbing) claim; shell and _single owe impl-drift only if make claims-owed says so.
decisions.why: Project process for a new code unit. It changes nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: Unit tests that list-form shell equals the joined string form and that the fixture's single page links its URLs; SC-001 and SC-002 run once over the real record and recorded in research.md rather than as a permanent gate test; make done; bookends.
decisions.why: The unit tests enforce FR-002 and the spec's edge case, and SC-002 names the small-record test itself. The one-shot real-record comparison is what SC-001 and SC-002 ask for and narrows neither. The bookends are constitution VI.
